## The lab exam

| | |
|---|---|
| Task | "Write R code to perform a series of analyses on a dataset and interpret the results" (syllabus) |
| When | Week 11, in class, at the normal lecture time; 2 hours |
| Weight | 30% of the course grade |
| Allowed | Any resources |

You get a dataset and run an analysis from start to finish: clean the variables, describe them, test associations, estimate models, and say in words what the results mean. The lab sessions prepare you for it, and Lab 6 (week 12) goes through the correction.

## How to use this guide

The pages follow the steps of an analysis, in the order you'd run them in the exam. Every section has the same four parts:

1. **Recipe:** the general code, with placeholders (`dataset`, `y`, `x`, `group`). The exam dataset may not be one from the labs, so start from the recipe.
2. **Example from the labs:** the lab code with its real output.
3. **How to read it:** what the numbers mean, and a sentence you can adapt for your answer.
4. **Your turn:** the labs' own exercises. Write the code yourself before you open the solution. Recalling it yourself sticks better than rereading it.

The [cheat sheet](cheatsheet.qmd) puts all the recipes on one page, to keep open during the exam.

## An analysis in five steps

This is the workflow from the labs:

| Step | Question | Typical commands | Page |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1. Inspect | What values does the raw variable contain? Which codes mean "missing"? | `table(x, useNA = "ifany")`, `summary(x)`, `sort(unique(x))` | [Start and clean](01-start-clean.qmd) |
| 2. Clean | Make a new variable; keep the original unchanged | `ifelse()`, `case_when()`, `factor()` | [Start and clean](01-start-clean.qmd) |
| 3. Verify | Did the recode work? | `table(new, useNA = "ifany")`, `table(old, new)` | [Start and clean](01-start-clean.qmd) |
| 4. Describe | What does the clean variable look like? | `table()`, `prop.table()`, `mean()`, `sd()`, `median()`, `hist()` | [Describe one variable](02-describe.qmd) |
| 5. Analyse | Which test or model fits the variable types? | `chisq.test()`, `t.test()`, `cor()`, `lm()`, `glm()` | pages 3–5 |

## Which test or model?

| Your variables | Use | Page |
|---|---|---|
| Two categorical variables | Crosstab with percentages, chi-square test | [Two variables](03-two-variables.qmd#two-categorical-variables) |
| A continuous variable and a binary group | Group means, t-test, boxplot | [Two variables](03-two-variables.qmd#a-continuous-variable-by-group) |
| Two continuous variables | Correlation, scatter plot | [Two variables](03-two-variables.qmd#two-continuous-variables) |
| Continuous outcome, several predictors | Linear regression (OLS) | [Regression](04-regression.qmd) |
| Binary outcome (0/1) | Logistic regression, marginal effects | [Logit and interactions](05-logit-interactions.qmd#logistic-regression) |
| Categorical outcome with 3+ categories | Multinomial logistic regression | [Logit and interactions](05-logit-interactions.qmd#multinomial-logistic-regression) |
| "Does the effect of x depend on z?" | Interaction term `x * z` | [Logit and interactions](05-logit-interactions.qmd#interactions) |

## The data



The examples and exercises use the two datasets from the labs. The site uses small extracts with only the lab variables, and the values are unchanged:

- [anes_lab.csv](data/anes_lab.csv): **ANES 2024**, US election survey, 5,521 respondents (Labs 1–3).
- [ess_lab.csv](data/ess_lab.csv): **European Social Survey round 11**, 39,514 respondents in 23 countries (Labs 4–5).
- [students.csv](data/students.csv): the student marks table from Lab 1.

In your own script, read the full files from Moodle instead, e.g. `read.csv("anes_timeseries_2024_csv_20250808.csv")` or `read.csv("ess.csv")`. The variable names are the same.
